what_everyone_knows: SMPL has had a rough 18 months: four straight quarters of YoY revenue decline (-0.3% to -9.4%), a five-year ~800bps gross-margin decline (40.7%->33.3% TTM), a $391.9M cumulative goodwill/brand impairment across three of the last four quarters, a CEO/CFO/Controller reshuffle inside 12 months, and a $280.2M debt-funded acquisition (OWYN) now 71% written off within 24 months. The stock trades at $11.33, well below its own five-year multiple history, and consensus (8 analysts, mean target $14.88) already models meaningful undervaluation with a 4-Buy/7-Hold split [final_thesis.md §4].
what_is_priced_in: The market is pricing a normalized FCF decline of roughly 9%/year for six straight years (or, equivalently, an 11.4% steady-state EBIT margin held near today's trough indefinitely) — a materially harsher and longer path than either company guidance (which only covers 1-2 years), Street consensus (FY2027 -4.5%, still being cut), or even this engine's own labeled worst-case structural-reset scenario, which still sits above today's price [valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md §2-§3, §5].
what_market_may_be_missing: That the LENGTH of the priced-in decline (six unbroken years) is arithmetically harder to justify than the visible evidence supports: Quest, 63.7% of nine-month FY2026 revenue and the dominant driver of the whole investment case, is still gaining household penetration (+120bps YoY to 20.5%, a multi-year high) even as the consolidated business shrinks, the September-2026 price increase and easing Atkins comps (both flagged by management) are not yet reflected in any reported quarter, and the balance sheet carries no maturity wall and $197.8M of liquidity against $0 near-term obligations — this is a 'does the turnaround land' question, not a 'does the company survive' question [final_thesis.md §4].
evidence_engine_is_different: There is limited genuine differential evidence. The engine's own §4 admits the 8-analyst mean target price ($14.88) sits within 3% of the engine's own base case ($15.27) — the analyst community already models a broadly similar fair value using its own methods, so this is a restated, well-triangulated consensus view rather than a proprietary insight the sell side has missed. The one piece of evidence that is somewhat differential — and not obviously already priced by the Street — is the reverse-DCF's own internal finding that even the engine's labeled worst-case structural-reset bear ($13.09) sits above the current price, meaning the market's downside case is more severe than the engine's own explicitly-constructed worst case; this is a real, citable, quantitative tension, but it is a single data point built from the engine's own model, not independent third-party confirmation that consensus has mispriced anything. No contrarian data source, alternative dataset, or channel check independent of the same Capital IQ/filing base every analyst also uses was cited. Final_thesis.md itself assigns an edge_score of 35/100 and states this 'is closer to a restated, well-triangulated consensus view than a proprietary edge' [final_thesis.md §4].
base_rate_check: The claim under test is SMPL's own forward FCF/EBIT-margin trajectory, tested at the correct level (consolidated, since no brand-level profit disclosure exists) and against the correct unit (FCF growth vs. FCF growth, margin vs. margin) — no metric/level/period mismatch. The base rate itself is genuinely mixed, not one-sided: SMPL's own FY2021-2025 pre-decline history (+9.6%/yr revenue CAGR, +5.8%/yr FCF CAGR) argues the priced-in 6-year continuous decline is an exceptional forecast, but the last four reported quarters (accelerating YoY declines, -0.3% to -9.4%) are the most recent, and most decision-relevant, realized data and they point the other way — toward continuation, not reversal, of the recent trend. FY2027 consensus is still being cut in every trailing window (revision breadth -4 to -6), which is itself evidence the market's skepticism has not stopped building. The engine's own §9 (base-rate discipline) read here is not that the market is making an exceptional forecast without exceptional evidence — a 1-2 year continuation of the current decline is well evidenced by guidance and consensus — but that a full SIX-year unbroken continuation, with no partial recovery even after two management-flagged levers (Sept-2026 price increase, easing Atkins comps) take effect, goes beyond what the visible 1-2 year evidence supports. This is a real, cited base-rate argument, but it rests on inference about years 3-6 that no one — including the engine — has direct evidence for yet.
